description: The Snowflake SELECT * column-list modifiers over a three-column fixture: EXCLUDE drops the listed columns and accepts a single column with or without parentheses; RENAME changes the OUTPUT NAME and leaves the value alone; REPLACE swaps the VALUE and keeps the name; ILIKE keeps only the columns whose names match the pattern; and a plain star is unaffected by any of it. Converted 1:1 from query/SelectStarModifiersTest (now retired); the Java asserted the column COUNT and sampled a name or two, so the converted tests pin both the full column list and the row, which is what separates RENAME from REPLACE.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sm (aa INTEGER, ab INTEGER, bc INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE sm (aa INTEGER, ab INTEGER, bc INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE sm (aa INTEGER, ab INTEGER, bc INTEGER)
SELECT * RENAME (aa AS x) FROM sm
CREATE TABLE sm (aa INTEGER, ab INTEGER, bc INTEGER)
SELECT * REPLACE (aa + 100 AS aa) FROM sm
CREATE TABLE sm (aa INTEGER, ab INTEGER, bc INTEGER)
